intro: This document updates the 57 test cases of STP-CCFD-1.1 (section 5) to match the system as built in Sprints 1 and 2. Each case keeps its ID, objective and traceability; where a sprint changed what a case checks, the case says what changed and why, with a reference to docs/DEVIATIONS.md. Two cases are new (TC-JOB-07, TC-MET-06), giving 59 in total.

Every case except TC-SAFE-04 is automated: the *Automated test(s)* row names the pytest test that executes it. Results are in the System Validation Report. Environment for all cases: Python 3.12+ (DEVIATIONS D-01).

history.change: Updated after Sprints 1 and 2: exact error messages, test substitutions, resolved TBD-03, two new cases

TC-SEC-01.title: Dataset upload without API key → 401, nothing stored
TC-SEC-01.objective: The upload endpoint rejects unauthenticated callers and stores nothing.
TC-SEC-01.preconditions: Server healthy; Authorization header deliberately omitted.
TC-SEC-01.steps: 1. POST /api/datasets with valid_1000.csv and no Authorization header. 2. List the datasets/ directory of the dataset store.
TC-SEC-01.expected: HTTP 401 with a {code, message} JSON body; the store is unchanged.
TC-SEC-01.pass: 401 received and no new file in the store.

TC-SEC-02.title: Invalid API key → 401
TC-SEC-02.objective: A wrong key is treated the same as a missing key.
TC-SEC-02.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-SEC-02.steps: 1. POST /api/datasets with valid_1000.csv and header Authorization: Bearer invalid- key-123.

TC-SEC-03.title: Analysis start without API key → 401, no job created
TC-SEC-03.objective: Job creation is protected; no phantom jobs appear.
TC-SEC-03.steps: 1. POST /api/analyses with {"dataset_id":"<id>","model_type":"ml"} and no Authorization header. 2. List the jobs/ directory of the dataset store and the microservice access logs.
TC-SEC-03.expected: HTTP 401; no job record created; no microservice request.
TC-SEC-03.pass: 401 received; no new job record; no new microservice request.

TC-SEC-04.title: Malformed JSON rejected before model processing, never logged
TC-SEC-04.objective: Strict schema validation stops malformed input at the server; payload contents never reach logs or microservices.
TC-SEC-04.steps: 1. POST /api/analyses with the truncated body {"dataset_id":. 2. POST /api/analyses with {"dataset_id":"<id>"} (model_type missing). 3. POST /api/analyses with {"dataset_id":"<id>","model_type":"ml","debug":true} (unknown field). 4. Inspect the application log and the microservice access logs.
TC-SEC-04.expected: HTTP 400 with a reason-naming body for all three requests; no job created; no payload fragment in any log; no microservice activity.
TC-SEC-04.pass: 400 on all three; logs contain no payload fragments; microservices show no new requests.

TC-SEC-05.title: Executable disguised as CSV rejected
TC-SEC-05.objective: File-type validation blocks non-CSV content regardless of the extension.
TC-SEC-05.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-SEC-05.steps: 1. POST /api/datasets with evil.csv (a binary executable renamed to .csv).
TC-SEC-05.expected: HTTP 400 naming "unsupported file type"; nothing stored; no microservice contacted.
TC-SEC-05.pass: 400 with the specific reason; store unchanged.
TC-SEC-05.change: Expected now quotes the exact message: `unsupported file type: the file is not CSV text` for binary content with a .csv name (`only .csv files are accepted` for other extensions). (source: DEVIATIONS D-12)

TC-SEC-06.title: Oversize upload rejected with specific reason
TC-SEC-06.objective: The 500 MB limit is enforced with a clear message.
TC-SEC-06.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-SEC-06.steps: 1. Upload a file larger than 500 MB. If this is impractical in lab time, temporarily lower the configured limit (for example to 5 MB), upload a larger file and record the substitution.
TC-SEC-06.expected: HTTP 400 with "file exceeds the 500 MB limit" (or the substituted limit); nothing stored.
TC-SEC-06.pass: 400 with the size reason; store unchanged.
TC-SEC-06.change: Automated run uses a 100 KB size limit instead of 500 MB (STP 13 substitution). Expected message: `file exceeds the 500 MB limit` (100 KB in the test). (source: DEVIATIONS T-03)

TC-SEC-07.title: Error responses disclose no internals
TC-SEC-07.objective: Client-facing errors and job failure reasons never leak stack traces, paths or configuration.
TC-SEC-07.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-SEC-07.steps: 1. GET /api/analyses/{random-uuid} → expect 404. 2. POST /api/analyses with malformed JSON → expect 400. 3. Make the dataset store directory read-only, upload valid_1000.csv → expect 500, then restore permissions. 4. Read the failure reason of a failed job from TC-JOB- 05.
TC-SEC-07.expected: Every body contains only {code, message} (or the job's reason object); no Traceback, file- system path, .py reference or configuration value.
TC-SEC-07.pass: None of the forbidden strings appear in any response.

TC-SEC-08.title: No transaction data in logs, UI or export
TC-SEC-08.objective: Transaction field values are never logged, displayed or exported (data display policy).
TC-SEC-08.preconditions: A completed ML job on extra_cols.csv (it contains a synthetic card_ref column).
TC-SEC-08.steps: 1. Search the application and microservice logs for distinctive values from extra_cols.csv (feature values and card_ref strings). 2. Inspect the results table and the downloaded CSV. 3. Upload non_numeric.csv and read the error message.
TC-SEC-08.expected: No field value appears in any log; the table and CSV show only row index, predicted class and fraud probability (no card_ref or feature column); the error message names the column and row but not the cell value.

TC-SEC-09.title: Dataset store permissions and 24-hour retention
TC-SEC-09.objective: Stored data is isolated on disk and deleted when its retention period ends.
TC-SEC-09.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-SEC-09.steps: 1. Upload valid_1000.csv and complete one job on it. 2. Check the permissions of the dataset store directory and its files. 3. With the retention period temporarily configured to 5 minutes (substitution recorded), wait until it has elapsed. 4. List datasets/, jobs/ and results/; GET the job.
TC-SEC-09.expected: Owner-only permissions for the service account; after the retention period the dataset file, job record and result file are deleted and GET returns 404.
TC-SEC-09.pass: Permissions are owner-only and all three artefacts are removed after the period ends.
TC-SEC-09.change: Step 3: retention 2 s and purge interval 0.2 s in the automated run (was 5 minutes). Owner-only permissions are checked on Linux and macOS; on Windows the store inherits the profile ACL. (source: DEVIATIONS T-03, D-07)

TC-SEC-10.title: Results retrieval without API key → 401
TC-SEC-10.objective: Results of a job cannot be read without a valid key, even when the job_id is known.
TC-SEC-10.steps: 1. GET /api/analyses/{job_id} with no Authorization header. 2. Repeat with Authorization: Bearer invalid-key-123.
TC-SEC-10.expected: HTTP 401 for both; no predictions or metrics in the body.
TC-SEC-10.pass: 401 on both requests and no result data returned.

TC-UPL-01.title: Valid dataset accepted and registered
TC-UPL-01.objective: A well-formed labeled CSV is accepted with a unique dataset identifier.
TC-UPL-01.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-01.steps: 1. POST /api/datasets with valid_1000.csv; record status, body and elapsed time. 2. Upload the same file again.
TC-UPL-01.expected: HTTP 201 with a non-empty dataset_id and rows = 1000, returned within 2 s; the second upload receives a different dataset_id.
TC-UPL-01.pass: 201 with dataset_id; elapsed ≤ 2 s; the two identifiers differ.

TC-UPL-02.title: Missing Class column → 400 naming the reason
TC-UPL-02.objective: Schema validation catches the missing label column with a specific message.
TC-UPL-02.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-02.pass: 400 with the column named; nothing stored.
TC-UPL-02.change: Expected now quotes the exact message: `missing required column: Class`. (source: DEVIATIONS D-12)

TC-UPL-03.title: Non-binary Class values → 400
TC-UPL-03.objective: The label domain (0/1 only) is enforced.
TC-UPL-03.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-03.change: Expected now quotes the exact message, which also names the data-row number: `invalid value in column Class at row N: Class must be 0 or 1`. (source: DEVIATIONS D-12)

TC-UPL-04.title: Header-only file → 400
TC-UPL-04.objective: A file with no data rows is rejected.
TC-UPL-04.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-04.expected: HTTP 400 stating that the file has no data rows.
TC-UPL-04.change: Expected now quotes the exact message: `the file has no data rows`. (source: DEVIATIONS D-12)

TC-UPL-05.title: Empty file → 400
TC-UPL-05.objective: A zero-byte upload is rejected gracefully.
TC-UPL-05.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-05.steps: 1. Upload empty.csv (0 bytes). 2. Repeat TC-UPL-01 step 1.
TC-UPL-05.pass: 400; the subsequent valid upload still returns 201.

TC-UPL-06.title: Wrong delimiter → 400
TC-UPL-06.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-06.expected: HTTP 400 naming the format problem as the reason.
TC-UPL-06.change: Expected now quotes the exact message: `wrong delimiter: the file must be comma-delimited`. (source: DEVIATIONS D-12)

TC-UPL-07.title: Non-numeric feature value → 400
TC-UPL-07.objective: Required feature columns must be numeric.
TC-UPL-07.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-07.change: Expected now quotes the exact message, which names column and row: `non-numeric or missing value in column <col> at row N`. (source: DEVIATIONS D-12)

TC-UPL-08.title: Extra columns tolerated and ignored
TC-UPL-08.objective: Files with columns beyond the documented schema are accepted and the extra columns are ignored.
TC-UPL-08.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-UPL-08.steps: 1. Upload extra_cols.csv. 2. Run an ML job on it and poll to completion.
TC-UPL-08.expected: HTTP 201; the run completes; predictions cover all rows.
TC-UPL-08.pass: 201 and a completed run with the correct row count.

TC-MOD-01.title: Run blocked with no model selected
TC-MOD-01.objective: The UI enforces model selection before execution.
TC-MOD-01.preconditions: Web Client open; API key entered; a dataset uploaded.
TC-MOD-01.steps: 1. Leave the model selector empty and activate the run control.
TC-MOD-01.expected: The run does not start; a message asks the user to select a model.
TC-MOD-01.pass: No POST /api/analyses is sent (browser network panel); the guidance message is shown.

TC-MOD-02.title: ML selection routes to the ML microservice
TC-MOD-02.objective: Selecting ML executes the ML service and labels results accordingly.
TC-MOD-02.traceability: REQ-FD-06, REQ-FD-07, REQ-FD-10, REQ-FD-11, REQ-FD-17, BR-03
TC-MOD-02.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MOD-02.steps: 1. POST /api/analyses with {"dataset_id":"<id>","model_type":"ml"}. 2. Poll to completion; check the ML service access log and the model_name.
TC-MOD-02.expected: 202 with job_id; the ML service received the request; the completed job's model_name is the classifier configured for the ML service.
TC-MOD-02.pass: 202; ML service called; model_name matches the configuration.

TC-MOD-03.title: DL selection routes to the DL microservice
TC-MOD-03.objective: As TC-MOD-02 for the DL option.
TC-MOD-03.traceability: REQ-FD-06, REQ-FD-08, REQ-FD-10, REQ-FD-11, REQ-FD-17, BR-03
TC-MOD-03.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MOD-03.steps: 1. Run with model_type "dl"; poll to completion; check the DL access log and model_name.
TC-MOD-03.expected: 202; completed job; model_name identifies the DL (MLP) model.
TC-MOD-03.change: The DL model is a scikit-learn MLPClassifier (64 and 32 ReLU units); expected model_name is `mlp`. (source: DEVIATIONS D-05)

TC-MOD-04.title: QML selection routes to the QML microservice
TC-MOD-04.objective: As TC-MOD-02 for the simulator-backed QML option.
TC-MOD-04.traceability: REQ-FD-06, REQ-FD-09, REQ-FD-10, REQ-FD-11, REQ-FD-17, BR-03
TC-MOD-04.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MOD-04.steps: 1. Run with model_type "qml" on valid_1000.csv; poll to completion.
TC-MOD-04.expected: 202; completed job (the simulator may be slower, which the asynchronous design absorbs); model_name identifies the QML model.
TC-MOD-04.pass: 202; completed with the QML model name.
TC-MOD-04.change: TBD-03 resolved: the QML model is a 4-qubit variational quantum classifier on PennyLane `default.qubit`; expected model_name is `vqc_4qubit`. (source: DEVIATIONS D-06)

TC-MOD-05.title: Unknown model_type → 400
TC-MOD-05.objective: The model-type enumeration is enforced at the API boundary.
TC-MOD-05.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MOD-05.expected: HTTP 400 naming the invalid model type; no job created.

TC-MOD-06.title: Microservice contract tested in isolation
TC-MOD-06.objective: Each microservice honours the uniform contract on its own, without the Web Server.
TC-MOD-06.preconditions: valid_1000.csv placed in the dataset store under a known dataset_id by the test fixture.
TC-MOD-06.steps: 1. GET /health on ports 5001, 5002 and 5003. 2. POST /predict with the known dataset_id to each service. 3. POST /predict with an unknown dataset_id.
TC-MOD-06.expected: 200 {"status":"ok"} from each health check; 200 with model_name, predictions and metrics in the contract shape; 404 with {code, message} for the unknown identifier.
TC-MOD-06.pass: All three services satisfy all three checks.

TC-JOB-01.title: Valid run accepted within 2 s with job_id
TC-JOB-01.objective: Analysis runs are asynchronous: the server accepts and returns at once.
TC-JOB-01.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-JOB-01.steps: 1. POST /api/analyses with {"dataset_id":"<id>","model_type":"ml"}; measure the time to response.
TC-JOB-01.expected: HTTP 202 within 2 s with a non-empty job_id and status "queued".

TC-JOB-02.title: Poll observes queued → running → completed in order
TC-JOB-02.objective: The full job lifecycle is observable and ordered; the client needs no reload.
TC-JOB-02.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-JOB-02.steps: 1. Start an ML run from the Web Client. 2. In the browser network panel, record each GET /api/analyses/{job_id} response and its time; watch the status badge.
TC-JOB-02.expected: Polls every 2 s; states progress queued → running → completed; the badge updates without a reload; polling stops at the terminal state.
TC-JOB-02.pass: All three states seen in order, polling interval 2 s (± 0.5 s), no manual refresh, no polls after completion.

TC-JOB-03.title: Unknown job_id → 404
TC-JOB-03.objective: Polling a nonexistent job returns a clean 404.
TC-JOB-03.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.

TC-JOB-04.title: Two concurrent jobs stay independent
TC-JOB-04.objective: Concurrent jobs do not interfere and each result set stays with its own dataset and model.
TC-JOB-04.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-JOB-04.steps: 1. Upload valid_1000.csv and valid_51.csv. 2. Start an ML run on the first and a DL run on the second back-to-back. 3. Poll both to completion; GET both jobs again 30 minutes later.
TC-JOB-04.expected: Two distinct job_ids; both complete; each job reports its own dataset_id, model_type and model_name, with 1,000 and 51 predictions respectively, and still does so later in the retention period.
TC-JOB-04.pass: Both complete with correctly associated results; no cross-contamination.
TC-JOB-04.change: Step 3: both jobs are read again immediately after completion instead of 30 minutes later; retention is tested by TC-SEC-09. (source: DEVIATIONS T-04)

TC-JOB-05.title: Microservice down → job failed; other services unaffected
TC-JOB-05.objective: An unavailable service yields a failed job with a reason — never fabricated results — and the other services keep working.
TC-JOB-05.steps: 1. Start a run with model_type "qml" from the Web Client. 2. Poll until a terminal state. 3. Start an ML run on the same dataset.
TC-JOB-05.expected: The QML job becomes failed with reason MODEL_SERVICE_ERROR; the Web Client shows the reason and no predictions or metrics; the ML job completes normally.
TC-JOB-05.pass: failed with reason and no results shown; ML run completes.

TC-JOB-06.title: Job timeout → failed with reason
TC-JOB-06.objective: The 600 s limit fires; hung jobs cannot linger.
TC-JOB-06.preconditions: A stub microservice that never responds, registered as the ML service.
TC-JOB-06.steps: 1. Start a run against the stub. 2. Poll past the configured timeout (a lower value, for example 30 s, may be configured; record the substitution).
TC-JOB-06.expected: The job transitions to failed with reason JOB_TIMEOUT.
TC-JOB-06.change: Automated run uses a 1 s timeout instead of 600 s (STP 13 substitution). The timeout is a hard overall deadline on the whole call. (source: DEVIATIONS T-03, D-11)

TC-JOB-07.title: Jobs interrupted by a server restart are marked failed
TC-JOB-07.objective: No job stays queued or running for ever after the Web Server restarts.
TC-JOB-07.preconditions: A job record left in state running by a stopped Web Server process.
TC-JOB-07.steps: 1. Stop the Web Server while a job is running. 2. Start it again. 3. GET the job.
TC-JOB-07.expected: The job is failed with reason MODEL_SERVICE_ERROR; no results are shown.
TC-JOB-07.pass: Job state failed with the reason; client polling stops.
TC-JOB-07.change: New in v1.2: covers the restart behaviour added during Sprint 2 (source: DEVIATIONS D-10).

TC-MET-01.title: Metrics correct to four decimals against an independent reference
TC-MET-01.objective: The five metrics match an independently computed reference.
TC-MET-01.preconditions: Completed ML job on valid_1000.csv; reference_metrics.json computed by a separate script from the same predictions.
TC-MET-01.steps: 1. Read the metrics from GET /api/analyses/{job_id}. 2. Compare each value with the reference.
TC-MET-01.expected: accuracy, precision, recall, f1 and roc_auc present, each with four decimal places, matching the reference.
TC-MET-01.change: The API returns probabilities with 6 decimals (the UI shows 4); the comparison stays at 4 d.p. (source: DEVIATIONS D-09)

TC-MET-02.title: Confusion-matrix counts are consistent
TC-MET-02.objective: The confusion matrix is complete and arithmetically consistent.
TC-MET-02.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MET-02.steps: 1. Read confusion_matrix from a completed job.
TC-MET-02.expected: Integer tp, tn, fp and fn whose sum equals the dataset row count.
TC-MET-02.pass: tp + tn + fp + fn equals the input row count.

TC-MET-03.title: Metrics and confusion matrix displayed and labeled with the executed model
TC-MET-03.objective: The results screen shows the metrics and confusion matrix, always identified by their source model.
TC-MET-03.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MET-03.steps: 1. Complete one run per model type from the Web Client. 2. Inspect each results screen and metrics payload.
TC-MET-03.expected: Each screen shows the five metrics and the four confusion-matrix counts, matching the API payload, labeled with the model_name of that job.
TC-MET-03.pass: All three runs display complete, correctly labeled metrics.

TC-MET-04.title: Same dataset across ML, DL and QML yields comparable metric sets
TC-MET-04.objective: Comparing approaches on identical data works end to end.
TC-MET-04.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MET-04.steps: 1. Run all three model types on valid_1000.csv. 2. Collect the three metric sets.
TC-MET-04.expected: Three complete metric sets with identical structure, computed over the same row count.

TC-MET-05.title: Hand-computed tiny dataset matches exactly
TC-MET-05.objective: End-to-end metric correctness on a dataset small enough to verify by hand.
TC-MET-05.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-MET-05.steps: 1. Upload tiny_4row.csv, run ML, read the predictions, metrics and confusion matrix. 2. Compute the metrics by hand from the returned predictions and the labels.
TC-MET-05.expected: Values match the hand computation (to 4 d.p.).
TC-MET-05.pass: Exact match on all five metrics and all four counts.

TC-MET-06.title: Single-class dataset: ROC-AUC reported as not available
TC-MET-06.objective: Metrics stay correct and honest when the dataset has only one class.
TC-MET-06.preconditions: A dataset whose Class column contains only 0.
TC-MET-06.steps: 1. Run the metric calculation on labels of one class only. 2. Read accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and ROC-AUC.
TC-MET-06.expected: No division error; ROC-AUC is null in the API and shown as n/a in the UI; the other metrics are defined.
TC-MET-06.change: New in v1.2: ROC-AUC is undefined without both classes (source: DEVIATIONS D-08).

TC-RES-01.title: Predictions table: columns and 50-row pagination
TC-RES-01.objective: The results table shows the required columns, paginated.
TC-RES-01.steps: 1. Open the results view; inspect the columns and the pager.
TC-RES-01.expected: Columns row index, predicted class and fraud probability; 50 rows per page; 20 pages for 1,000 rows.
TC-RES-01.pass: Columns correct; 50 rows per page; 20 pages.

TC-RES-02.title: Pagination boundary: 51 rows → 2 pages
TC-RES-02.objective: The page boundary drops or duplicates no rows.
TC-RES-02.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-RES-02.steps: 1. Run on valid_51.csv; open the results; count the rows on pages 1 and 2.
TC-RES-02.expected: Page 1 has 50 rows and page 2 has 1 row; row indices are continuous.
TC-RES-02.pass: 50 + 1 rows with no gaps or duplicates.

TC-RES-03.title: Prediction value domains
TC-RES-03.objective: Every row receives a valid class and probability.
TC-RES-03.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-RES-03.steps: 1. Read the full predictions array of a completed job on valid_1000.csv.
TC-RES-03.expected: One prediction per input row; class ∈ {0, 1}; probability ∈ [0, 1].
TC-RES-03.pass: Count matches the input; all values in domain.

TC-RES-04.title: Results appear automatically when the job completes
TC-RES-04.objective: The Web Client moves from status to results on its own.
TC-RES-04.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-RES-04.steps: 1. Start a run in the browser; do not reload or click anything further.
TC-RES-04.expected: The status badge moves through queued → running → completed, and the predictions table and metrics appear automatically on completion.
TC-RES-04.pass: Results shown with no reload or extra user action.

TC-RES-05.title: Error message adjacent to control within 1 s
TC-RES-05.objective: Errors are shown where they happened, promptly.
TC-RES-05.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-RES-05.steps: 1. In the browser, upload no_class_column.csv; in the performance panel, measure from receipt of the 400 response to the message appearing; note its position.
TC-RES-05.expected: The message appears next to the upload control within 1 s of the server response.

TC-RES-06.title: CSV download: columns and row count
TC-RES-06.objective: Completed predictions are downloadable in the specified shape.
TC-RES-06.steps: 1. Use the download control; open the CSV.
TC-RES-06.expected: Columns row index, predicted class and fraud probability; one row per transaction.
TC-RES-06.pass: Exactly the three columns; 1,000 data rows.

TC-RES-07.title: Single-page layout, upload control, help link and 1280×720 viewport
TC-RES-07.objective: All controls are on one page, the upload control takes one file, guidance is always reachable and the layout works at the minimum viewport.
TC-RES-07.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-RES-07.steps: 1. Open the Web Client; confirm the API-key field, upload control, model selector, run control and results region are on one page. 2. Try to select two files in the file chooser. 3. Check the help link in every state of the page and open it. 4. Resize the viewport to 1280×720 and walk the upload → run → results flow.
TC-RES-07.expected: All controls on one page; the chooser accepts a single file; the help link is visible in every state and opens the manual; all controls reachable with consistent styling at 1280×720.

TC-API-01.title: POST /api/datasets contract
TC-API-01.objective: The upload endpoint's success contract is exact.
TC-API-01.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-API-01.steps: 1. POST /api/datasets with valid_1000.csv; inspect status, headers and body.
TC-API-01.pass: 201 with the exact body shape and JSON content type.

TC-API-02.title: POST /api/analyses contract
TC-API-02.objective: The analysis endpoint's acceptance contract is exact.
TC-API-02.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.

TC-API-03.title: GET /api/analyses/{job_id} contract
TC-API-03.objective: Status polling returns the documented job shape in every state.
TC-API-03.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-API-03.steps: 1. GET a running job, a completed job and a failed job (from TC-JOB-05); inspect the bodies.
TC-API-03.expected: 200 with job_id, dataset_id, model_type and status in every state; model_name, predictions and metrics only when completed; reason {code, message} only when failed.
TC-API-03.pass: Shape correct in all three states.

TC-API-04.title: Uniform error body
TC-API-04.objective: All errors share the uniform body shape.
TC-API-04.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-API-04.steps: 1. Trigger 400 (bad upload), 401 (no key) and 404 (unknown job). 2. Inspect each body.
TC-API-04.expected: Each body is {"code": "<MACHINE_CODE>", "message": "<text>"} with JSON content type, using the codes listed in SADS Section 3.3.
TC-API-04.pass: Uniform shape and documented codes on all three.

TC-API-05.title: Wrong HTTP method → 405
TC-API-05.objective: Method enforcement on the API surface.
TC-API-05.preconditions: Server healthy; requests carry the test API key.
TC-API-05.expected: HTTP 405 with the uniform error body for both.

TC-PERF-01.title: Upload result within 2 s for up to 10,000 rows
TC-PERF-01.preconditions: Single-host deployment on the reference machine; client on the same host so transfer time is negligible.
TC-PERF-01.steps: 1. Upload valid_1000.csv and perf_10k.csv with curl -w %{time_total}; repeat each 3 times. 2. Repeat with a 10,000-row file that has a missing Class column.
TC-PERF-01.expected: Each 201 or 400 response arrives within 2 s.

TC-PERF-02.title: Status polling p95 ≤ 500 ms under 10 concurrent pollers
TC-PERF-02.objective: The status endpoint stays responsive under concurrent polling.
TC-PERF-02.preconditions: A running job; the 10-client polling script.
TC-PERF-02.steps: 1. Launch 10 concurrent pollers for 60 s against GET /api/analyses/{job_id}. 2. Compute the response-time distribution.
